title: Quarterly hypothesis-driven roadmap: Private/VPC/on‑prem activation cadence and OKR mapping
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Purpose: produce a compact, testable quarterly roadmap for Private/VPC/on-prem features that ties directly to OKRs: activation velocity, time-to-first-request, and isolation reliability. This ticket scopes a hypothesis-driven approach: list high-impact experiments, a tranche activation plan for enterprise cohorts, gating criteria, and measurable acceptance signals for each milestone.

Scope: feature areas covered include onboarding automation (network templates + quickstart), RBAC and audit logging parity with Hosted, KMS/HSM integrations for customer-managed keys, upgrade windows and rollback tooling, and observability exports for tenant-level SLIs. Also coordinates with runtime teams on autoscaling and kernel/quantization compatibility needed for known customer workloads.

Goals (quarter):
- Reach end-to-end activation for 3 pilot customers on Private with <3 business-day setup for VPC tenants (OKR: activation_velocity).
- Demonstrate stable tenant isolation under load: P95 tail latency degradation <10% vs baseline and no cross-tenant KV pollution (OKR: reliability_isolation).
- Deliver documented upgrade & rollback playbook exercised in at least one on-prem pilot (OKR: operational_maturity).

Hypotheses to validate this quarter: 
H1: Providing pre-built VPC network templates + a guided console flow will reduce setup time by >50% for pilot customers.
H2: A gating checklist that requires RBAC + audit log ingestion before activation reduces post-activation security issues by >70%.
H3: Coordinated autoscaling profile recommendations tied to model family will lower median CPU/GPU utilization by 20% for pilot workloads while preserving latency SLOs.

Milestones & rough timeline: 
- Week 1-3: Define activation playbook + customer cohort criteria; build template library and onboarding checklist.
- Week 4-6: Deliver RBAC & audit-log parity work to console with test fixtures; run internal attack surface review.
- Week 7-9: Ship KMS/HSM integration alpha and docs; enable key rotation testing with pilot.
- Week 10-11: Run end-to-end pilot activations for 3 customers and collect metrics.
- Week 12: Synthesize learnings, update OKRs, and decide roll/shelve for next quarter.

Gating & rollout policy:
- Must pass security checklist (RBAC roles verified, audit log ingestion validated) before enabling production traffic.
- Autoscaling recommendation engine must provide per-tenant profile suggestions; if runtime misses memory threshold, fallback to smaller concurrency mode.
- Rollout is tranche-based: dark-launch to internal -> pilot customers (3 cohorts) -> wider beta. Each tranche has acceptance criteria and a go/no-go review.

Acceptance signals (what success looks like):
- Activation_time <= 72 hours for 3 pilot customers (measured from contract signed to first successful inference).
- No security incidents from pilot activations for 30 days post-activation.
- Console telemetry shows per-tenant cost estimate accuracy within ±15% of actual for first 30 days.
- Upgrade runbook executed with successful rollback (if needed) on at least one on-prem instance.

Deliverables:
- Playbook doc (Confluence) and one-click network template bundle.
- Console onboarding flow + RBAC audit checklist.
- KMS/HSM alpha integration and test harness.
- Pilot activation report + metrics dashboard and recommended next steps.

Success criteria and next decisions:
- If activation_velocity and reliability_isolation targets met -> scale to 10 pilot customers next quarter and prioritize automation of billing/account mapping.
- If not met -> identify top two blockers (network, RBAC, runtime perf) and schedule tactical engineering sprints for Q2.
acceptance_criteria: Security checklist validated for each pilot before production traffic
P95 latency degradation <10% vs baseline under pilot load
Upgrade/rollback playbook executed successfully on an on-prem instance
